classification.difficultyReason: Link supplementary cyclic angles in one circle, a straight-line angle and the alternate-segment theorem in the second, then recognise the parallel-line criterion.

content.prompt: Choose $T$ on the smaller circle. Let $FTG$ be the tangent at $T$ and construct lines $KAT$ and $TBL$ as shown in the diagram. Let $\angle LKT=\theta$.

spec.description: Two intersecting circles; K,A,T and L,B,T are secants, AB is extended and FTG is tangent to the smaller circle.
spec.mathematics: Circle intersections A/B are computed exactly from centres/radii; K/L are second intersections of TA/TB with larger circle; FTG is perpendicular to small-circle radius at T.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens, named points and unknowns; no calculated answers.

answer.worked:
Since $K,A,T$ are collinear, $\angle LKA=\theta$. In cyclic quadrilateral $KABL$,
$$\angle LBA=180^\circ-\theta.$$
Since $L,B,T$ are collinear, $\angle TBA=\theta$. The alternate segment theorem in the smaller circle gives
$$\angle GTA=\angle TBA=\theta.$$
$\angle LKT=\angle GTA=\theta$. These are equal alternate angles on transversal $KAT$, so $LK\parallel FG$.
